THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE E.S.INDIRESH
ORAL JUDGMENT
Heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties.

2. This appeal is arising out of the judgment and award dated 14.02.2022 in MVC No.1223/2018, on the file of Motor Accident Claims Tribunal No.XV, Vijayapura (hereinafter referred to as 'Tribunal'),
awarding compensation.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal No.XV, Vijayapura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. For the sake of brevity, the parties in the appeal shall be referred to in terms of their status and ranking before the Tribunal.
NC: 2026:KHC-K:989 HC-KAR 4.

The relevant facts for adjudication of the claim petition are that, on 23.06.2018, the claimant was riding his motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-25/R-1696 near Preeti Dhaba on Yakkundi - Jamakhandi road and at that time, the driver of Bolero Goods Vehicle bearing registration No.KA-23/A-6973, applied the break suddenly and on account of the same, the motorcycle of the claimant dashed to the back portion of the Bolero vehicle.
As a result of the same, the claimant sustained injuries.
Hence, the claimant has preferred MVC No.1223/2018 seeking compensation.
5. The claim petition was contested by the respondents therein.

In order to establish their case, the claimant has examined two witnesses as PW.1 and PW.2 and produced 14 documents and the same Pavan @ Pavankumar vs Siddaling Buran Bastawade And Anr on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138002888/
2 were marked as Exs.P1 to P14.

entities.text: Pavan @ Pavankumar vs Siddaling Buran Bastawade And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Respondent No.2 - Insurance Company has examined RW.1 and marked two documents and the same were marked as Exs.R1 and R2.

The Tribunal after considering the material on record, by its judgment and NC: 2026:KHC-K:989 HC-KAR award dated 14.02.2022, awarded compensation of Rs.1,52,200/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization.
Insofar as liability is concerned, the Tribunal has arrived at a conclusion that, respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation.
However, respondent No.2 - Insurance Company was directed to pay the compensation and thereafter, recover the same from respondent No.1.
It is also forthcoming from the impugned judgment and award that, the contributory negligence was made to an extent of 50:50.
Feeling aggrieved by the same, the claimant has preferred this appeal.

6. Sri Sanganabasava B. Patil, the learned counsel appearing for the appellant submitted that, the Tribunal has committed an error in arriving at a conclusion that, the claimant has contributed 50%
towards alleged accident, which is required to be interfered with in this appeal.
It is also argued by the counsel appearing for the NC:
2026:KHC-K:989 HC-KAR appellant also argued for enhancement of compensation as made by the Tribunal.
7. Per contra, Smt.Preeti Patil Melkundi, the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2 - Insurance Company sought to justify the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

8. In the light of the submission made by the learned counsel appearing for the parties, it is not in dispute that, on 23.06.2018, the claimant has sustained injuries on account of the alleged accident.

Perusal of the police records, particularly, the charge sheets at Exs.P5 and P6 makes it clear that, the claimant while riding the motorcycle, has hit the Bolero vehicle from behind and therefore, I am of the view that, the liability fixed to the extent of 50% is just and proper, which does not call for interference.
9. Insofar as award of compensation is concerned, the Tribunal has erred in considering the disability to the NC: 2026:KHC-K:989 HC-KAR extent of 5%.

By looking into the injuries sustained by the claimant, I am of the view that, the Tribunal ought to have taken the disability at 10% and therefore, applying the appropriate multiplier of 18, by taking into consideration the monthly income of the claimant at R.11,750/-, the claimant is entitled for Rs.2,53,800/-
(Rs.11,750x12x18x10%) towards loss of future income.

10. Taking into account the injuries sustained by the claimant, the award of compensation by the Tribunal is reassessed as follows:
 Heads Amount Pain and suffering Rs.50,000/-
Loss of earnings during laid up Rs.35,250/-
period (Rs.11,750x3)
Loss of amenities Rs.10,000/-
Loss of future of earnings Rs.2,53,800/-

sentences.text:
Towards food and nourishment Rs.10,000/-
Towards attendant charges Rs.10,000/-
Medical expenses Rs.1,07,090/-

Total Rs.4,76,140/-
Less: awarded by Tribunal Rs.1,52,200/-
Enhancement Rs.3,23,940/-
 NC: 2026:KHC-K:989 HC-KAR
Thus, the clamant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.3,23,940/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum.

11. In the result, I pass the following:
ORDER I.
The appeal is allowed in part.
II. The appellant/claimant is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.3,23,940/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
III. Respondent No.2 - Insurance Company is directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
IV. In all other aspects, no interference is called for insofar as the liability and apportionment of the compensation is concerned.
NC: 2026:KHC-K:989 HC-KAR V.
Taking into consideration the order dated 31.01.2024, the claimant is not entitled for interest, for the delayed period of 328 days in filing the appeal.
